attackVerdicts.attack: DB1 — bunScrubbedSpawner `extra` spread defeats the ScrubbedEnv brand: extra:{env:process.env} overrides the branded env at runtime
attackVerdicts.evidence: O1 probe against the REAL production bunScrubbedSpawner: control scrubbed spawn → child sees runtime=absent; extra:{env:{...process.env with RUNTIME_KEY}} → child sees runtime=sk-runtime-FAKE. Source scrubbed-spawn.ts:74-84 destructures {…,extra} and spreads `...(extra ?? {})` AFTER `env:`, so extra.env wins. extra is typed Readonly<Record<string,unknown>> — 'MUST NOT carry an env' (line 61) is a comment, not a type. The brand is not the structural backstop R1 claims; the census is.

attackVerdicts.attack: DB2 — R1's proposed ratchet predicate (argv head ∈ LSP_SERVER_BINARIES) matches NEITHER real LSP spawn site
attackVerdicts.evidence: transport.ts:73 spawns `this.command` (PropertyAccessExpression, no local initializer); availability.ts:28 spawns `[bin,'--version']` (Identifier head from a param). exec-cluster test argvHeadIsShell (lines 376-404) resolves only string literals + local-initialized identifiers, fail-closed otherwise. R1's own anti-vacuity assertion ('transport.ts and availability.ts IN population') would FAIL under R1's predicate. Post-fix both are caught only because routing through the funnel trips the EXISTING IMPORTS_FUNNEL predicate — so the argv-head extension is both unnecessary for the fixed state and unable to catch a NEW literal-argv LSP spawn in a non-funnel file.

attackVerdicts.attack: DB3 — per-server initializationOptions hardening does NOT close the .cargo/config.toml rustc-wrapper RCE; only the RUSTC_WRAPPER='' env delta does
attackVerdicts.evidence: O2 via real RustAnalyzerAdapter+LspTransport in repo cwd: wrapper-rel:none → 20 execs of ./wrap.sh; wrapper-rel:init (R1 hardened initOptions ONLY) → 12 execs (STILL LIVE); wrapper-rel:init+env (adds RUSTC_WRAPPER='') → 0. R1 hellgate #2 mutates only buildScripts.enable, so the entire env-delta half of the rust fix can be deleted and the test stays green. EXTENDED: I found TWO more init-immune rust RCE vectors — (a) .cargo/config.toml [build] rustc=./evil (rustc-cfg): init+env → 12 execs, only RUSTC=<trusted abs> pin → 0; (b) rust-toolchain.toml absolute-path toolchain: init+env (repo cwd) → 1 exec + server crash, only RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=<default> pin → 0. init options close build.rs alone.

attackVerdicts.attack: DB4 — LSP_ENV_ALLOWLIST is a divergent hand-rolled allowlist that drops HOME/RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME the rustup proxy needs
attackVerdicts.evidence: rust-analyzer on this machine is ~/.cargo/bin/rust-analyzer → symlink to rustup (a proxy). O2 shows the hardened cases WORK (server started, def resolved) only because RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME/HOME were kept; the proxy exports RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN to children (rt probe) and resolves the toolchain via RUSTUP_HOME. R1's PATH+locale+SSL+TMPDIR-only set would break the proxy launch ('rustup could not choose a version', the artifact seen in P4's first run). env-scrub.ts already has DEFAULT_ENV_ALLOWLIST + CI_ENV_ALLOWLIST, and git-runner/runner.ts:7 adds a 4th ALLOWED_ENV — MEMORY's 'no sixth parallel model' applies. But the LSP list genuinely must DIFFER from DEFAULT (drop PYTHONPATH/VIRTUAL_ENV/PYTHONHOME/NODE_OPTIONS which are pyright/node exec vectors, ADD RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME) — so it should be DERIVED from the SSOT with per-var justification, not a fresh copy, and MUST keep the rustup-home vars.

r1ClaimCorrections.claim: availability.ts:28 Bun.spawn([bin,'--version']) 'omits env entirely (inherit-by-omission FULL env)' — a full-env leak, severity high
r1ClaimCorrections.correction: WRONG as stated. Bun 1.3.14 env-less spawn passes the process LAUNCH-env snapshot, NOT live process.env. O1: env-less child saw launch=sk-launch-FAKE (exported before bun) but runtime=absent (set after start). A credential loaded from .env.dev at runtime (loadEnvFiles, src/apps/cli/index.ts:33 — MEMORY sep-04) does NOT reach the availability child; only a shell-exported cred does. The availability leak is REAL but strictly weaker than 'full env'. The TRANSPORT leak is the strong one: transport.ts:86 passes buildLspServerEnv(process.env,…) = LIVE env, so dotenv creds DO leak — every O2/O3/O4 probe set the key at runtime and the child saw it. Any test that proves the availability leak by mutating process.env at runtime is vacuous.

revisedDesign.summary: Make the LSP LAUNCH itself safe so the read-only nav tools AND the mention resolver can both stay prompt-free. Single hardened launch chokepoint = LspTransport.spawn routed through the existing scrubbed-spawn funnel with an LSP-derived allowlist + per-server env delta + trusted binary/interpreter resolution + per-server no-exec initializationOptions. The env-scrub + trusted-toolchain + no-exec init ship DEFAULT-ON and trust-INDEPENDENT (probes show they reduce every proven vector to 0); TrustStore only RE-WIDENS rust-analyzer buildScripts/procMacro fidelity for a trusted repo (no decline/null path, so the non-null create() type and the mention path both stay intact). Same 'stop the exec + stop the credential leak at the funnel' shape as 4ebe02c71 (shadow_verify) and e0c1912c0 (node-repl), applied to the interactive+mention LSP path those commits skipped.
revisedDesign.structuralMechanism: (1) One hardened launch PORT: LspTransport.spawn goes through bunScrubbedSpawner so its env is the branded ScrubbedEnv — an unscrubbed LSP spawn is a tsc error; the funnel's `extra` bug is sealed first so the brand actually holds. (2) A location/import CENSUS ratchet (not argv-head): any Bun.spawn under src/lsp/** or src/agent/lsp-bridge/** must route through the funnel — makes an unscrubbed LSP spawn impossible to reintroduce regardless of argv shape. (3) One SSOT: an exhaustive Record<LspServerKind, HardeningSpec> (initializationOptions + envDelta + resolveTrustedBinary + resolveTrustedInterpreter) with a runtime drift guard, wired into a new initializationOptions channel on initialize. (4) Trusted resolution: a findTrustedCommand-style resolver (mirror Codex trustedPath: absolute, reject paths under cwd / containing node_modules|.venv) is the single authority for both the server binary and the python interpreter.

userDecisions.question: U1 — Ship env-scrub + trusted binary/interpreter + no-exec init + RUSTC/RUSTUP/RUSTC_WRAPPER pins DEFAULT-ON and trust-independent, or behind a knob?
userDecisions.options: default-on (matches buildLspServerEnv/node-repl/shadow_verify security fixes) with QUANTA_LSP_HARDENED=0 opt-out | opt-in knob
userDecisions.recommendation: Default-ON, trust-independent, with a QUANTA_LSP_HARDENED=0 escape for a trusted power user who needs build-script symbols. This closes a credential leak + multi-vector RCE that fires out-of-box, including on the mention path with nav tools disabled.

userDecisions.question: U2 — rust-analyzer buildScripts/procMacro: OFF always, or OFF-untrusted / ON-trusted?
userDecisions.options: OFF always | OFF for untrusted, ON for trusted (TrustStore) | ON always (status quo RCE)
userDecisions.recommendation: OFF for untrusted, ON for trusted. Never ON for an untrusted repo. This is fidelity re-widening layered on the always-on safety base, not a decline path — so the non-null create() type and the mention path are unaffected.

userDecisions.question: U3 — Trusted-binary/interpreter resolution strictness: reject any resolved path under cwd / containing node_modules|.venv (Codex trustedPath), or recompute PATH from a trusted allow-set?
userDecisions.options: reject-workspace-paths (Codex trustedPath) | recompute PATH from trusted dirs only | both
userDecisions.recommendation: reject-workspace-paths as the primary (simplest, matches Codex main-D87AK7lw.js:91219 and O6's need), with the resolved absolute path passed as argv[0]. This is NEW plumbing (not in R1) and needs sign-off on the exact rejection predicate — it changes which binary launches on a dev who activated a repo venv.

userDecisions.question: U4 — OS-sandbox (seatbelt/landlock) wrap of the LSP process?
